principle: Mobile reuses the desktop Prompt Kit data, filters, renderers, and action functions. Responsive behavior may reorganize layout or expose explicit touch controls, but it must not create a second interaction model.

requirements.expected: The main Prompt Kit title/logo is a pointer- and keyboard-accessible reset control that restores All prompts, All Categories, All Types, empty search, closed detail/reference surfaces, and the top of the page.
Every prompt card exposes an explicit Open action so touch users do not depend on double-click or double-tap timing to inspect prompt detail.

The whole non-control surface of every prompt card remains a tap/click-to-copy target on touch/coarse-pointer and pointer layouts. The explicit Copy action remains visible and touch-sized, but it is a secondary affordance rather than a requirement to reach the terminal clipboard action. A card tap copies through canonical copyPrompt acknowledgement and must not open prompt detail.

On narrow mobile layouts, a persistent touch-sized Favorites quick action remains visible outside horizontally scrollable rails and opens the existing canonical Favorites view without creating separate Favorites state or storage.

When Favorites contains saved prompts in one or more existing prompt sections, the Favorites view exposes a compact touch-usable Saved groups navigator built from those existing rendered sections and counts. Activating a group jumps to that section without changing Favorites membership, creating collection state, or using browser Find.

Favorites saved in the existing canonical browser storage survive a page reload. An empty Favorites view distinguishes: no saved IDs, saved IDs unavailable in the current prompt registry, and available saved Favorites hidden by current filters. Recovery actions must be useful for each state, unknown imported IDs remain preserved for portability, and clearing filters must never change membership.

On narrow touch layouts, a persistent Go to P# control is the fastest locator when the user already knows a prompt ID. The user taps Go to P#, enters digits only (for P111, type 111), and an exact unambiguous ID reveals and instant-snaps its canonical prompt card into the actionable viewport with prompt detail closed, without opening More, browser Find, or a search-result step. The landed card itself is the primary terminal copy surface: tapping any non-control area copies the canonical prompt; explicit Copy remains available and explicit Open is reserved for deliberate inspection. When an exact ID is also a prefix of a longer prompt ID (for example P11 versus P111), it must not steal the longer route: the status says the shorter ID is exact, the submit control becomes Go to P11, and Enter or that button deliberately jumps to P11 while continued typing can reach P111. Prefix-only or nonexistent IDs have no enabled exact-submit target; canonical P00-P09 IDs require their leading zero; pasted values such as P111 normalize to the same digits-only resolver. A separate compact More control exposes Find Prompt, previous/next profile, Search, Favorites, Filters, Reference, Top, and Bottom as labeled buttons. Swiping is not required and no hidden gesture vocabulary is part of the primary phone interaction contract. Desktop Hotkeys and shared semantic actions remain authoritative; phone controls do not create parallel prompt state. Go to P# must never auto-open the space-heavy detail modal merely to expose Copy.

Mobile interaction identity is derived from the touch/coarse-pointer medium rather than viewport width alone. The same loaded phone page preserves Go to P#, More, touch action rails, and hidden desktop reference handles across PORTRAIT -> LANDSCAPE -> PORTRAIT without reload or state reset. Width may still compress layout geometry inside a mode, but rotating a phone must not switch it to desktop controls. Conversely, a narrow or unusually tall desktop viewport may reflow content but retains desktop Hotkeys and the bottom-right Reference handle and must not expose mobile-only controls.
Library, category, and type filters remain the same controls and semantics; narrow layouts may present them as horizontally scrollable touch rails rather than wrapping into an unstable header.
Narrow layouts render prompt cards in one readable column without horizontal page overflow.

Prompt detail reuses the existing detail surface and functions but is entered only through an explicit inspection action such as Open, not by Go to P#. When deliberately opened it occupies the mobile viewport with an accessible close and full-width Copy action and exposes the canonical Favorite toggle; favoriting there or on the card updates the same Favorite state without a second shortcut-save step.
The existing reference panel remains available and expands to the mobile viewport rather than introducing a separate reference UI.
Top/Bottom links remain present and touch-usable on every visible prompt category without changing active filters.

Open-Latest-PromptKit.cmd provides a zero-dialog normal-user route that resolves Desktop/OneDrive development roots, preserves unsafe existing work, safely syncs canonical main, validates exact Prompt Kit parity, and opens the canonical website.

proof_ceiling: Static source, deterministic tests, generated-site parity, CI, and exact-head Chromium journeys prove the tracked responsive/browser behavior they exercise, including Go to P# snap-without-detail, whole-card tap copy, explicit Open inspection, the exact/prefix, leading-zero, pasted-ID, and missing-ID edge-case matrix, a same-page 390x844 -> 844x390 -> 390x844 phone orientation cycle, and a narrow/tall desktop control-identity regression. Physical Android thumb reach, real software-keyboard timing, browser-specific clipboard prompts, hybrid-device primary-input heuristics, and device-specific viewport/browser UI remain field acceptance gates.
